newsitem.title: USA: U.S West spot power mixed on temperatures, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S West spot power mixed on temperatures, natgas.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. were mixed amid cooler temperatures in the Northwest and stronger natural gas prices, market sources said Friday.
"Prices will probably be up more on Monday," said one Northwest trader.
He said colder weather will likely drive real-time prices higher early next week when schedulers move to cover near-term needs.

Hydroelectric supplies in the Northwest are deemed plentiful, but Bonneville Power Administration's emphasis on locking up most of its surplus sales under term deals is expected to limit the agency's daily spot offers.
Firm, peak California-Oregon border (COB) electricity for Monday was assessed at $23.00-24.00 per megawatt hour (MWH), unchanged from Friday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Monday was slightly higher at $15.50-17.00.
Monday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was slightly higher at $21.00-22200. Off-peak Mid-C was little changed at $15.00-16.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Monday was quoted $22.00-23.00 per MWh, while off-peak PV was a little lower at $13.50-15.00.
Monday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were slightly lower at $22.00-23.00, while firm off-peak was assessed at $13.50-14.50.
